Defence stocks were among the top gainers on Friday, rising up to 17 percent amid strong investor interest, driven by stock-specific actions, fresh orders and a positive growth outlook for the second half of the fiscal year.

The rally pushed the Nifty India Defence index up nearly 4 percent. The index has gained for the third consecutive session, rising more than 5 percent during the period. Buying was seen across all 22 constituents of the index.

Bharat Electronics gained nearly 2 percent and emerged as the top gainer in the Nifty benchmark index.

BEML was the top performer in the Nifty India Defence index, surging nearly 17 percent to hit a 52-week high of Rs 2,378 per share on the NSE.

The sharp rally followed recent comments by Defence Secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh that the Defence Ministry is seeking a 20 percent increase in defence capital expenditure for FY28. He also said the winner of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme would be announced within about a month.

  • APL Apollo Tubes shares rise 3.5% after 30% rout; Tata Steel weighs options to address investor conc...

Three private-sector consortiums are competing for the AMCA programme. These include an L&T-Bharat Electronics-Bharat Dynamics consortium, a Bharat Forge-BEML-Data Patterns consortium, and Tata Advanced Systems as a standalone bidder.

Solar Industries India was another major gainer, rising more than 6 percent.

The stock gained after the company's subsidiary, Solar Defence and Aerospace Ltd (SDAL), completed in-house development trials of Bhargavastra, an indigenously developed two-layer, vehicle-mounted counter-swarm drone system.

The system combines a 64-tube air defence rocket launcher (Version-I) with a 64-micro-missile launcher (Version-II), featuring autonomous guidance and infrared seekers to engage multiple drones.

During an earnings call, the company said it expects to complete its internal trials and conduct field trials within the current calendar year, following which commercialisation would begin.

"There is a huge demand for such kind of products," the company said.

Meanwhile, Paras Defence and Space Technologies, Bharat Dynamics Ltd (BDL) and Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) gained between 3 percent and 6 percent.

HAL shares advanced after brokerage firm Elara Capital maintained its 'Buy' rating on the stock and raised its target price to Rs 6,270 from Rs 6,000. The revised target indicates an upside potential of nearly 28 percent from the stock's previous closing price.

Meanwhile, shares of Omnitech Engineering rallied as much as 5 percent after the company announced it received a development order from BrahMos Aerospace for assemblies and sub-assemblies of metallic airframe components and canister subsystems.

Harshit Kapadia, Vice President - Industrial, Defence, Railway, Consumer Electrical/Durables/Electronics at Elara Securities told CNBC-TV18, that the Ministry of Defence's Rs 1,980-crore agreement linked to Israel's Barak air defence system may lead to a large part of the programme to be indigenised, with Bharat Electronics and Bharat Dynamics likely to benefit from domestic manufacturing and missile production.

data.title: November rally triggers massive mutual fund redemptions; net inflows set to plunge
data.description:
November rally triggers massive mutual fund redemptions; net inflows set to plunge
  • Mutual funds face massive redemptions in November.
  • Investors book profits during the sharp market rally.
  • HNI investors exit to buy cheaper US tech stocks.

in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan

Mutual funds are set to end November with massive redemptions and significantly lower net inflows, as investors use the sharp market rally to book profits and exit their investments. Sources at fund houses and distribution firms told Moneycontrol that redemption activity has been unusually high this month, even as benchmark indices have surged more than 12%, putting them on course for their strongest monthly performance in over six years.

Sources at mutual funds and distribution firms told Moneycontrol that November has seen exceptional redemption activity, coinciding with the sharp recovery in frontline indices. The month is likely to end with significantly lower net inflows than in recent months, extending the moderation in equity mutual fund flows after they peaked in March 2026.

Equity-oriented mutual fund schemes attracted Rs 40,450 crore in March, the highest monthly inflow so far this year. The figure fell to Rs 32,994 crore in October, 18% below the March peak, after coming in at Rs 38,307 crore in September. October nevertheless marked the 68th consecutive month of net inflows into equity schemes.

Sources at AMCs, leading retail distributors and wealth advisors suggest the net inflow number for the month could come in around Rs 10,000 to Rs 15,000 crore, about 50-70% lower compared with October.

Redemptions have been lower from retail investors. Some of the leading retail distributors said their net inflows in November could end up roughly 30% lower than October. Redemption requests have been running substantially higher, they said, although the final numbers could improve as investors typically make fresh investments towards the end of the month. Fund houses, however, described the redemption pressure as more pronounced, with high-net-worth investors in particular looking to take money out after the sharp rebound.

Related Stories

  • Market goes Atmanirbhar as DIIs beat foreign peers in buying Indian equites, 3 years on
  • Five themes that are worth investing today: A handy guide by Trideep Bhattacharya, CIO, Edelweiss MF
  • SIP contributions hit record Rs 10,351 crore in September

HNI investors rush to exit

A key trigger for investors taking money out of the markets is also triggered in part by the allure of cheaper US tech stocks. The sharp correction in US technology stocks, particularly those linked to artificial intelligence, has attracted opportunistic interest from investors looking to buy into the decline, wealth managers said.

Nvidia, one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI investment boom, fell from an intraday high of $243.37 on October 6 to a low of $124.50 on November 20 — a decline of nearly 49%. The Nasdaq Composite, meanwhile, dropped from its record closing high of 27,599.79 on October 6 to an intraday low of 22,513.01 on November 20, a correction of about 18%.

The steep fall in technology stocks has prompted some investors to consider increasing or initiating exposure to US equities at lower valuations, wealth managers said. However, the extent to which overseas investments account for the rise in domestic mutual fund redemptions remains unclear.

Retail investors cash out

As for retail investors, the behaviour is not unusual. Investors often hold on to their investments when markets fall, but use a recovery to exit once losses have narrowed or portfolios have returned to breakeven. Such redemptions can also reflect a mismatch between investors' expectations and the actual performance and volatility of the asset class, or a realisation that they had invested in products that were not suited to their risk appetite.

In that sense, the churn need not be entirely negative. Investors who exit after a recovery may be replacing a short-term approach with a more considered allocation elsewhere. Over time, this could leave mutual funds with a more committed pool of long-term investors. But the immediate consequence is a moderation in fresh money coming into the market even as share prices rise.

The shift in domestic flows is also visible in the secondary market. Foreign portfolio investors have turned strong net buyers of Indian equities, purchasing shares worth Rs 1.28 lakh crore in the cash market in November through November 26. Domestic institutional investors, in contrast, were net sellers to the tune of Rs 54,898 crore over the same period.

The contrast is striking: foreign investors are returning to Indian equities as domestic institutions turn sellers, while some domestic mutual fund investors are using the rally to withdraw money. The November surge in benchmark indices may therefore be telling only one part of the story. Beneath the surface, investors seem to be clearly rethinking their equity calls and overall allocations.

Shares of APL Apollo Tubes rose 3.5 percent on Friday, extending the previous session's marginal gains after a sharp selloff earlier this week. The recovery comes as Tata Steel's management indicated that it was exploring ways to address shareholder concerns over the proposed transaction, without abandoning the acquisition.

APL Apollo Tubes shares rose to Rs 1,533 in afternoon trade, after losing approximately 30.2 percent over the previous three trading sessions. The stock had plunged 21.2 percent on Monday and another 11.6 percent on Wednesday, before recovering marginally by 0.4 percent on Thursday.

Despite the latest recovery, APL Apollo shares remain down 22.2 percent in 2026, significantly underperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined 1.7 percent during the period. The company's market capitalisation stood at approximately Rs 42,500 crore.

Tata Steel shares were also trading 0.6 percent higher at Rs 164.50 on Friday. The stock has declined 9.5 percent this year, with the steelmaker commanding a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 2.05 lakh crore.

  • APL Apollo, Hindustan Zinc, other metal stocks rally up to 3% as copper, aluminium prices recover
  • HEG shares list at 25% premium after demerger of graphite electrode business; stock hits 5% lower ci...

Tata Steel exploring ways to address shareholder concerns

Speaking to CNBC-TV18 earlier this week, Tata Steel CEO and Managing Director T V Narendran said the company was evaluating feedback from investors and discussing ways to improve the transaction structure.

Narendran indicated that the management would come back with a solution once it had found a way to address these concerns, acknowledging the urgency of the matter. However, he said it was too early to comment on whether another board meeting would be convened to consider changes to the transaction.

APL Apollo promoter Sanjay Gupta was equally concerned about minority shareholders and keen to find a solution, Narendran said, adding that Tata Steel also wanted to ensure that the interests of its own shareholders were protected.

The Tata Steel chief ruled out calling off the transaction for now, saying discussions were focused on improving its structure and that there was no indication of Gupta backing away from the deal either.

Narendran said the rationale behind the transaction structure was to retain APL Apollo as a separately listed company. He also indicated that the two companies intended to find ways to work together irrespective of the outcome of the proposed transaction.

Debt burden, earnings dilution remain key concerns

Brokerages have sharply lowered their valuations for APL Apollo following the announcement, citing higher leverage, earnings dilution, expensive acquisition valuations and the exit of its existing promoter.

ICICI Securities downgraded the stock to 'Sell' from 'Add' and cut its target price to Rs 1,345 from Rs 2,200. Axis Capital retained its 'Sell' rating and lowered its target price to Rs 1,420 from Rs 2,400, estimating that FY28 earnings per share could decline 52 percent and net debt-to-EBITDA could rise to around seven times. Nuvama downgraded the stock to 'Hold' with a fair value of Rs 1,459, citing similar concerns.

Tata Steel's Rs 32,266 crore acquisition plan

Tata Steel on Monday announced an agreement to acquire up to 26.38 percent of APL Apollo from a promoter group entity for approximately Rs 15,511 crore, triggering a mandatory open offer for another 26 percent stake at Rs 2,301.40 per share.

The combined outlay could reach Rs 32,266 crore, potentially taking Tata Steel's holding to 52.38 percent. As part of the transaction, nearly 10 percent of APL Apollo's equity changed hands in a Rs 5,825 crore block deal on Monday. The broader agreement involves APL Apollo acquiring Tata Steel's tubes business and Tata Steel Colors for up to Rs 28,000 crore in cash, with brokerages expecting the acquisition to be substantially debt-funded.

data.title: China stocks rally after rare midday statement on market support
data.description:
Beijing will improve policies guiding long-term funds into stocks and encourage listed companies to step up dividend payouts and share buybacks, according to the Xinhua News Agency

Chinese stocks rallied after the State Council reaffirmed its support for the market in a rare midday statement, emphasizing the role of the so-called national team and pledging to roll out more policies.

Beijing will improve policies guiding long-term funds into stocks and encourage listed companies to step up dividend payouts and share buybacks, according to the Xinhua News Agency. The CSI 300 Index, an onshore benchmark, rose more than 3%, while the chip-heavy Star 50 Index jumped about 12%, the most since October 2024.

The statement comes at a precarious time for Chinese stocks, with most equity benchmarks entrenched in a bear market amid tepid earnings and a weak economy. Even with the day’s gains, the CSI 300 Index has lost 13% so far in 2026, putting it on track for its worst year since 2022. While authorities sought to revive investor confidence through a slew of measures starting in October and state funds have been actively buying, they have mostly been seen as stemming the losses rather than engineering a recovery.

“The statement shows that stabilizing the capital market remains a priority at the highest levels of government, which should help ease negative sentiment,” said Fu Zhifeng, chief investment officer at Shanghai Chengzhou Investment Management. “After the recent selloff, investors have shown little appetite to buy the dip, while much of the selling pressure may have already been exhausted. The announcement can therefore provide further support to the market this afternoon.”

Tech stocks drove the rally on the CSI 300, with Cambricon Technologies Corp. and Zhongji Innolight Co. up more than 13%. AI-related stocks have been hit particularly hard in the latest downturn, with their frothy valuations coming under scrutiny as the US tightened its exports of high-end chips to China.

Shares of Le Lavoir hit the 5% lower circuit at Rs 39.72 apiece on BSE after the Securities and Exchange Board of India issued an interim order for fraudulent issuance of shares and warrants and attempts to manipulate the stock price by key management personnel. Only 294 shares of the company had changed hands.

The regulator alleged Le Lavoir Chairman Ashok Jain, Managing Director Sachin Kapse, and 12 other directors and entities were prima facie involved in the fraudulent issuance of shares and warrants on a preferential basis and attempts to manipulate the company's share price. According to the interim order, which will remain in force until further orders from SEBI, the company is prohibited from raising any further capital in any form. The chairman has also been directed not to buy or sell securities.

SEBI's examination of bank statements of certain preferential allottees indicated that their subscription amounts were allegedly funded directly or indirectly by Jain or entities connected with him.

Sonali Abhaykumar Parmar, allotted 60,000 warrants, received Rs 40 lakh from Jain and his wife through Kirti Dilipkumar Jain, identified as Jain's sister, to fund her Rs 39.71 lakh initial subscription. Parmar subsequently paid the amount to Le Lavoir.

V P Jaware Gowda, allotted 78,000 warrants, received Rs 31.38 lakh from Sheeba Swapna, an entity/person connected with Jain, which was transferred to Le Lavoir within minutes. This represented around 60.79 percent of his initial subscription amount.

SEBI noted that Jain, his family members and Parmar accounted for around Rs 6.21 crore, or 59.37 percent of the total initial subscription amount received by Le Lavoir.

SEBI flagged transfers involving Ghantiram Foods, Shree Vrajendra Foods and Ghura Industries, alleging funds moved through multiple entities before reaching Jain. It questioned a Rs 2.61 crore loan repayment to Dhanashree Electronics, noting no corresponding loan receipt in FY26 bank statements. Separately, Rs 1.55 crore was advanced to Ghura Industries, with portions subsequently routed through other entities.

SEBI flagged the discontinuation of arrangements with Hotel Fariyas and Hotel Tunga, whose subsequent developments were allegedly not disclosed to stock exchanges.

The regulator also said certain traders connected with Jain allegedly contributed to price increases through small trades, including single-share first trades above the previous day's closing price. It referred to earlier proceedings involving Jain and Darjeeling Industries Ltd.

The findings are prima facie observations in an ex-parte interim order. The noticees have been given 21 days to submit replies and seek a hearing.

Online food and grocery delivery company Swiggy is set to lay off 340 employees from its quick commerce division, Instamart, as it restructures the business for its next phase of growth, amid a rise in AI adoption, people aware of the developments told Moneycontrol. Shares of Coforge Ltd rose 3.5 percent to Rs 2,070 in morning trade on Friday, November 27, recovering their previous session's losses after private equity firm Advent International dismissed speculation over an imminent stake sale in the IT services company.

Coforge shares had plunged around 6 percent in intraday trade on Thursday to hit a nearly one-month low of Rs 1,945.6 after a media report said entities owned by Advent International were looking to offload around 10 percent stake in the company through block deals. The stock subsequently recovered some of its losses to settle 2.91 percent lower at Rs 2,000 on Thursday.

No block deal in Coforge shares had been reported as of Friday morning.

Advent International dismisses stake sale speculation

CNBC-TV18 reported on Thursday, citing unidentified sources, that entities owned by Advent International were likely to sell around 10 percent stake in Coforge through block deals to institutional investors. Two investment banks had reportedly been appointed to manage the proposed transaction, which was expected to take place soon.

Related Stories

  • Le Lavoir shares hit 5% lower circuit as SEBI issues interim order
  • Nifty IT snaps 4-day winning streak on profit booking; HCL Tech, TCS lead losses: Here's how to trad...
  • Gold, silver rate rebound: Precious metals-linked stocks rally up to 4%; Muthoot Finance, Titan, Hin...

  • Share Markets Live Updates | Sensex, Nifty, GIFT Nifty Today

However, Advent International later clarified that it remained a committed and active shareholder in Coforge. The US-based private equity firm also termed the speculation regarding imminent block trade transactions in the IT services company as unfounded.

Entities owned by Advent International currently hold around 20 percent stake in Coforge. At the company's current market capitalisation of around Rs 91,700 crore, a 10 percent stake would be valued at approximately Rs 9,170 crore.

Advent's share lock-in period to expire on November 30

The speculation over a potential stake sale comes ahead of the expiry of the mandatory six-month lock-in period on Advent International's shares in Coforge on November 30. Coforge had allotted the shares to Advent International on a preferential basis at Rs 1,815.91 apiece in April. The allotment followed the IT services company's announcement in December 2025 that it would acquire Encora at an enterprise value of $2.35 billion.

At Friday's prevailing market price, Coforge shares were trading around 14 percent above the preferential allotment price.

While the expiry of the lock-in period would enable Advent International to sell its shares, it does not necessarily imply an immediate stake dilution.

Coforge share price performance

Coforge shares have gained around 25 percent so far in 2026, significantly outperforming the benchmark Nifty 50, which has declined around 1.1 percent during the same period. Friday's rebound has also taken the stock marginally above Wednesday's closing price of Rs 2,060, erasing the losses triggered by the stake sale report.
